newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: LOW TURNOUT EXPECTED IN CZECH SENATE RUN-OFF-PAPER.
newsitem.headline: LOW TURNOUT EXPECTED IN CZECH SENATE RUN-OFF-PAPER.

text.p: A low turnout is expected in the second round of Czech Senate elections on Friday and Saturday, according to an opinion poll reported by the daily Mlada Fronta Dnes on Friday.
"Our survey shows that the turnout will be the same or even lower than the last week," the daily quoted Jan Herzmann, analyst with polling agency Factum, as saying.
Low turnout, which in the first round was only 35.03 percent, has helped the senior coalition partner, the Civic Democratic Party (ODS) of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus.
Herzmann said that 31 percent of the population had firmly decided to vote and another 15 percent were considering participating in the election.
In the first round last week ODS candidates won 36.47 percent of the total vote, far ahead of the second most successful party, the opposition Social Democrats, who got 20.27 percent.
Referring to the likely low turnout in the runoff, Herzmann said: "That is why I am convinced the coalition will win the elections."

Candidates will compete for 77 of the Senate's 81 seats. Four candidates won more than half the first round vote in their constituency, meaning they do not have to face the runner up in the second round.
